question: Is the measured synchronous-query reduction worth accepting the explicit long-lived database ownership invariant that every enabled handle must clear cached native statements before it is closed, repaired, replaced, or evicted?
rationale: The patch is intentionally bounded and documented, but the native statement-to-database retention behavior creates a cross-cutting lifecycle obligation that ordinary focused query tests cannot permanently enforce for future owner paths.

options.title: Confirm lifecycle ownership and merge
options.body: Accept the cache after confirming that all shared and per-agent enabled-handle disposal funnels remain routed through clear-before-close helpers and required CI passes.

options.title: Keep uncached execution
options.body: Decline the cache if the ongoing ownership burden is not acceptable relative to the benchmarked gateway-event-loop reduction.

options.title: Narrow the cache further
options.body: Limit activation to a smaller proven hot path if maintainers want performance benefit with a smaller lifecycle surface.

recommendation.title: Confirm lifecycle ownership and merge
recommendation.body: Accept the cache after confirming that all shared and per-agent enabled-handle disposal funnels remain routed through clear-before-close helpers and required CI passes.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-head follow-up commits and audit comment directly address the cache lifecycle and disposal ownership question.
